title: ‘You Don’t Put Your Head in the Sand for 4 Years’: Colossal CEO Ben Lamm on Working With Trump
gist: Colossal Biosciences CEO Ben Lamm explained at WIRED World Fair how the company sold the Trump administration on a biobank of endangered-species DNA, defending the work against conservationist criticism. Colossal, valued at $10.2 billion, reportedly seeks a $20-30 billion valuation and will miss its 2028 mammoth deadline.

themes.theme: Selling biotech to the Trump administration

insights.claim: Lamm says the Trump administration likes technology, making and saving money, and exciting wins, and used that framing to win support for a government biobanking initiative to collect DNA from endangered species.
insights.speaker: Ben Lamm
insights.so_what: Pitching to administration priorities opens federal partnerships for deep tech.

insights.claim: Lamm defends working with the administration, saying dire biodiversity forecasts mean 'you don't put your head in the sand' for four years.
insights.speaker: Ben Lamm

insights.claim: Lamm says biobanking matters more than the headline de-extinction work as climate change and habitat destruction pressure wildlife.
insights.speaker: Ben Lamm
insights.so_what: Shows pivot toward conservation as the investable framing.

insights.claim: Colossal raised $230 million in its Series C last year at a $10.2 billion valuation, and per Axios is seeking a new round at $20-30 billion.
insights.speaker: Brian Kahn
insights.so_what: Valuation could double to triple on a story-driven biotech.

insights.claim: Colossal has spun out multiple companies, including a microbe-based plastic-destroying firm, and holds a stake in Warhound, developed with Anduril CEO Palmer Luckey, to make genetically enhanced working dogs for military, police and first responders.
insights.speaker: Brian Kahn

insights.claim: Lamm says the Warhound approach aims to reduce dependence on European 'puppy mills' that supply working dogs.
insights.speaker: Brian Kahn

insights.claim: Critics say Colossal oversells: its dire wolves have genomes very similar to gray wolves, and its announcements are more style than substance.
insights.speaker: Brian Kahn
insights.so_what: Scientific skepticism poses reputational and valuation risk.

insights.claim: Conservationists argue promising de-extinction could increase the odds of policies today that lead more animals to go extinct.
insights.speaker: Brian Kahn

insights.claim: Colossal will miss its initial 2028 deadline for a woolly mammoth, despite 130 edits to mammoth genes; Lamm is fine with calling creations 'hairy elephants'.
insights.speaker: Brian Kahn

insights.claim: Lamm says the company has 'undersold' its gene-editing efforts, promises more 'surprise and delight moments', and rules out megalodon work.
insights.speaker: Ben Lamm
insights.so_what: Expect more PR-driven announcements ahead of fundraising.
